title: Free representable module Ext is derived object evaluation
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site with its objects, arrows, covering indices and coefficient values in one universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], and let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. Use sheaves of $R$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For $U\in\mathcal C$ define $P_U(V)=\bigoplus_{a:V\to U}R(V)$, with restriction along $h:V'\to V$ sending $r e_a$ to $R(h)(r)e_{ah}$, and let $E_U=P_U^\#$ be module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], with unit $\eta:P_U\to E_U$. The category $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ has enough injectives. There is a natural additive isomorphism
$$\theta_N:\operatorname{Hom}_R(E_U,N)\xrightarrow{\sim}N(U),\qquad \theta_N(\alpha)=(\alpha\eta)_U(e_{\mathrm{id}_U}),$$
whose inverse sends $s$ to the unique sheaf map whose composite with $\eta$ sends $r e_a$ to $rN(a)(s)$. For any module map $b:N\to N'$ one has $\theta_{N'}(b\alpha)=b_U\theta_N(\alpha)$. For every $R$-module sheaf $M$ and $q\geq0$ there are canonical additive isomorphisms
$$\operatorname{Ext}_R^q(E_U,M)\cong R^q\Gamma_{\mathrm{Mod},U}(M)\cong H^q(U,M_{\mathrm{ab}}).$$
Here $M_{\mathrm{ab}}$ is the underlying abelian sheaf, $\Gamma_{\mathrm{Mod},U}(N)=N(U)$, and both module derived functors are computed by injective module resolutions [def-sp-injective-resolutions]: for any $M\to J^\bullet$, $\operatorname{Ext}_R^q(E_U,M)=H^q\operatorname{Hom}_R(E_U,J^\bullet)$ and the first comparison is induced by $\theta_{J^n}$ in every degree. The last term is right-derived evaluation in abelian sheaves [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology](2). The comparisons are natural in $M$ and in degree zero are $\theta_M$ followed by the identity on $M(U)$. No injectivity of $M_{\mathrm{ab}}$ or flatness of $R$ over $\mathbf Z$ is assumed.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck] to the given small site and ring sheaf $R$ in the common universe. Thus $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ is Grothendieck abelian, so [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] supplies enough injectives. The common universe contains all object and arrow sets, covering indices and coefficient values, exactly as required by the first result. We may therefore choose an injective module resolution $M\to J^\bullet$.

source.place: Tag 01DU, theorem-sheaves-modules-injectives; Grothendieck argument of Tag 079Q, remark-existence-D

proof.text: By [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification], precomposition with $\eta$ is a bijection from sheaf maps $E_U\to N$ to presheaf module maps $P_U\to N$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-free-yoneda-presheaf-module] to the latter maps: evaluation at $e_{\mathrm{id}_U}$ is a bijection with $N(U)$, with inverse $s\mapsto(r e_a\mapsto rN(a)s)$. Their composite is precisely $\theta_N$. It is additive since evaluation of $(\alpha+\beta)\eta$ at that basis vector is the sum of the two evaluations; the inverse of an additive bijection is additive. Finally $(b\alpha\eta)_U(e_{\mathrm{id}_U})=b_U((\alpha\eta)_U(e_{\mathrm{id}_U}))$, proving the stated naturality. Thus these maps form an additive natural isomorphism $\operatorname{Hom}_R(E_U,-)\cong\Gamma_{\mathrm{Mod},U}$.

Apply [lem-sc-ext-right-derived-cocycle-comparison] with $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$, $A=E_U$, $H=\Gamma_{\mathrm{Mod},U}$ and $e=\theta$. The additive natural isomorphism just constructed verifies its represented-functor hypothesis, and step 1 gives its injective resolutions. Its hypothesis that Ext is computed in the Hom universe $v$ of $\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ also holds: by [lem-weil-pbc-ext-via-injective-resolution], applied with an injective resolution $Y\to I^\bullet$ from step 1, $\operatorname{Ext}^n_R(X,Y)\cong H^n\operatorname{Hom}_R(X,I^\bullet)$, a subquotient of the $v$-small group $\operatorname{Hom}_R(X,I^n)$. Its normalized comparison, inverted, gives $\operatorname{Ext}_R^q(E_U,M)\cong R^qH(M)$. Explicitly, naturality with $b=d_J^n$ gives $\theta_{J^{n+1}}(d_J^n\alpha)=(d_J^n)_U\theta_{J^n}(\alpha)$, so $\theta$ identifies the Hom and evaluation complexes. The cited normalization sends every represented Ext cocycle to this evaluated cocycle class, giving exactly the asserted resolution formula. The cited natural isomorphisms also ensure independence of resolution and naturality in $M$. In degree zero, if $i:M\hookrightarrow J^0$ is the augmentation, $\theta_{J^0}(i\alpha)=i_U\theta_M(\alpha)$; identifying the kernels with $M$ gives $\theta_M$.

source.place: Tag 06XR, lemma-compute-ext-resolutions, part (1); applied to the Hom evaluation identification in sites-cohomology.tex, Tag 07AC

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-site-module-abelian-evaluation-comparison] to $(\mathcal C,R,M,U,q)$. Its universe and enough-injectives hypotheses were checked in step 1; it permits arbitrary ring sheaves. It supplies the second additive isomorphism $R^q\Gamma_{\mathrm{Mod},U}(M)\cong H^q(U,M_{\mathrm{ab}})$, natural in $M$ and the identity on $M(U)$ for $q=0$. Composing with step 3 gives all claimed comparisons and the degree-zero normalization. The cited statement expressly requires neither flatness over $\mathbf Z$ nor injectivity of the underlying abelian sheaf.
